title: Sync Your Fork with Upstream
description:
**SITUATION:**

You keep a **personal fork** of sprint-service for experiments. On this laptop that fork is what Git calls `origin`. The **Forgeboard org** project — the shared copy everyone treats as source of truth — is ahead of you: someone already landed an invite audit helper (`src/invite_audit.py`) on org `main`, and your fork's `main` does not have it yet.

Git only knows about remotes you configure. Right now you only have `origin` (your fork). The org project is not hooked up yet. The usual name for "the project I forked from" is `upstream`. You need to add that remote, bring org `main` into your local `main`, then push so **your fork** on `origin` catches up — otherwise work from your fork stays based on stale history.

Do **not** push commits onto the org `upstream` `main`. That remote rejects it on purpose. Your write target is only `origin`.

One more mess on the laptop: you once pushed `feature/card-colors` while trying board card colors, then deleted that branch on the fork. Your laptop still lists `origin/feature/card-colors` as a remote-tracking branch. After you sync, clean that stale pointer so your remote branch list matches what is actually on the fork.

Jordan asked you to wire up `upstream`, fast-forward your `main` to the org tip, publish that tip to your fork, and prune the ghost branch. Leave a clean working tree.

Your identity (Ada Learner) is already configured. Start on `main` in `~/sprint-service`; `origin` already points at your fork on `git.forgeboard.internal`.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Add the Forgeboard org repo as a remote named `upstream` (`learner@git.forgeboard.internal:/srv/git/forgeboard-sprint-service.git`).
2. Fetch from `upstream` and update your local `main` so it matches `upstream/main` (fast-forward only — you have no local commits to keep).
3. Push the synced `main` to `origin` so your fork catches up. Do not push to `upstream`.
4. Prune stale remote-tracking branches so `origin/feature/card-colors` is gone. End on `main` with a clean working tree.

hints: `git remote add upstream learner@git.forgeboard.internal:/srv/git/forgeboard-sprint-service.git` then `git fetch upstream`.
`git merge --ff-only upstream/main` (or rebase) while on main, then `git push origin main`.
Do not push to upstream — push your fork only.
`git fetch --prune origin` drops remote-tracking branches deleted on the fork.
problemStatement.overview: Your fork (`origin`) lags the org repo. Add `upstream`, fast-forward `main` from org, push the fork, prune deleted `origin/feature/card-colors`.
problemStatement.brief: Add `upstream`, ff-only sync `main` from org, push `origin`, prune stale `origin/feature/card-colors`.
problemStatement.solution:
# Solution — Sync Your Fork with Upstream

`origin` is your fork (behind). The Forgeboard org repo is not configured yet — add it as `upstream`, fast-forward local `main`, push the fork, then prune a branch already deleted on `origin`.

```bash
cd ~/sprint-service
git remote -v
git remote add upstream learner@git.forgeboard.internal:/srv/git/forgeboard-sprint-service.git
git fetch upstream
git switch main
git merge --ff-only upstream/main
git push origin main
git fetch --prune origin
git branch -r   # origin/feature/card-colors should be gone
```

Do not `git push upstream main` — the org remote rejects it.
